pr_title: ddl: supports transitions between time types
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #19122

What's Changed: Just bypass all type checks. And `column.go:L651` is needed to explicitly convert between different types.

### Check List

Tests

- Unit test
- Integration test

### Release note

- support column type change between the Time types
pr_comments:
> @xhebox  Please address the comments.

Got. I did not miss it. I am doing the placement rules project.

According to [this question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/409286/should-i-use-the-datetime-or-timestamp-data-type-in-mysql), the first difference of `DATETIME` and `TIMESTAMP` is that they've different ranges:

```
mysql> create table t(a datetime);
Query OK

mysql> insert into t(a) values ('1000-01-01 00:00:00');
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.46 sec)

mysql> 
mysql> alter table t modify a timestamp;
ERROR 1292 (22007): Incorrect datetime value: '1000-01-01 00:00:00' for column 'a' at row 2
```
So the type ranges are what we should check.

Another thing to notice is that `DATETIME` is timezone-aware while `TIMESTAMP` is not. So far as I found is that MySQL uses the current timezone to convert `TIMESTAMP` to `DATETIME`:

```
mysql> create table t(a datetime, b timestamp);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.03 sec)

mysql> set @@time_zone='+0:00';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> insert into t(b) values ('2009-05-08 17:00:00');
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> select * from t;
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-08 17:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> set @@time_zone='+8:00';                                                                                        
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t;                                                                                                
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-09 01:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> alter table t modify b datetime;
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.05 sec)
Records: 1  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> select * from t;
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-09 01:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> set @@time_zone='+0:00';                                                                                        
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t;                                                                                                
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-09 01:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> alter table t modify b timestamp;
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.09 sec)
Records: 1  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> select * from t;                                                                                                
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-09 01:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> set @@time_zone='+8:00';                                                                                        
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t;
+------+---------------------+
| a    | b                   |
+------+---------------------+
| NULL | 2009-05-09 09:00:00 |
+------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
I'm not sure if we are able to handle them correctly(without data-reoganzation) in TiDB, I will dig deeper.

> So the type ranges are what we should check.

Thx :). I am aware of that, though.. I am writing a script to help me identify mysql behaviors. The main problem blocking me is more on the backfiller: it is using `CastValue` to convert between different types, but the datum does not reflect the full infomation of a column type. E.g.:

```
create table t(c1 year, c2 time, c3 date, c4 datetime, c5 timestamp);
alter table t modify column c4 year;        # It should report an error.
```

The error is `E1292: incorrect datatime field`, looks like reported when converting to year. But TiDB seems lose the column infomation. For TiDB, it is trying to convert a string datum to year, without knowning the original column type.

 As a result, it is difficult to behave identically to mysql.

I could directly forbid all-fail cases of convertion before re-orgranization(`tiemstamp to year` will always fail). `year to time` and `datetime to timestamp` have a mixed situation. These two can only report error when invoking `table.CastValue`(at https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/8d798bbee1e2dd1121d9ac5b14e15fb190dbc22f/ddl/column.go#L1069). Reorg rollback code is at https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/ddl/column.go#L888-L898, which I did not found due to non-fetch-merge base branch...

But I still have a problem even with rollback. I did not found any `errCancelledDDLJob` error along the code path of `return w.updateColumnAndIndexes(tbl, oldCol, changingCol, changingIdxs, reorgInfo)`. Any truncated error will just keeps retrying and can not be cancelled, e.g. the comment https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/19988#pullrequestreview-490424808:

```
create table t(c1 year, c2 time, c3 date, c4 datetime, c5 timestamp);
alter table t modify column c1 date;        # It just stuck and keeps retrying and cannot be cancelled.
```

**EDIT**: Due to this problem, I did not check the conversion correctness of new added tests, yet.

The related 'cancel' state is actually `JobStateRollingback` because some clean-up tasks are handled by 'rolling back' process. Basically you can check the code [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/20032/files#diff-0ef842ac66131b78e2b1b259c81fc5f4L895).

issue_context.title: Supports transitions between the same type (Time types)
issue_context.body:
### Description

Supports transitions between the same types, including unsigned transitions.

### Value

- Support conversion between Time types
    + The DATE, DATETIME, and TIMESTAMP Types
    + The TIME Type
    +  The YEAR Type
comments: I am picking up this one.

Yeah, it is a good idea. L655 is already checking the flag.
